elimination.verdict: PASSES. Rule is zero items with any confidently rejectable option. Three solvers, all 30 items, all 120 options: legal==1 on 0 of 90 votes, any legal<4 on 0 of 90. All three reached it independently and by the same reasoning — a bare lexical option carries no proposition to contradict, no set holds a synonym or subsumption pair (the near-misses are ANTONYM pairs, which kill nothing), and every option is a well-formed completion of some stem. Each explicitly refused to count the cluster/singleton shape as an elimination, recording legal:4 and calling it a lean.

tells.verdict: The singleton inversion was MEASURED rather than argued. The three elimination solvers deliberately bet against the singleton on every item and scored 26/90 = 28.9%, against the original singleton rule at 16.7% and a 33.3% ceiling for picking uniformly from the three cluster members. So the axis carries real information — inverting gains 12.2 points over the singleton rule — but a student who learns the inversion gains only +3.9 over chance and lands well short of the ceiling, meaning that within the cluster there is no signal at all. Recorded as a batch-level shape with no automated guard, of the same family as the "identical key prose across lectures" case, and fed forward to s11: the inversion should not be this consistent across a whole form.

tells.verdict: FAILS, on a defect no structural check can see and the attack cannot reach: SUBJECT RECALL. All three graders volunteered it unprompted and independently. The author chose booming dunes because there is no scientific consensus to recall, and all three confirmed that premise is CORRECT and is not what protects an item — what protects it is whether the key coincides with the prior. The two rival accounts (a dry-layer acoustic waveguide over a denser substrate; shear-rate x grain-diameter collision synchronisation) are each well documented, and the batch assigns one camp per passage, so recognition routes by camp without any consensus existing. Counts: grader A 3 of 9 outright plus 2 partly, grader B 3 of 9, grader C 2 decisive plus 2 assisted. All three name P1-Q4 and P1-Q9 in the cluster. One grader notes that P1-Q9s option set is the CLEAN shape — four parallel "Sound is produced only while X" frames varying one term — so the leak there is recall, not axis-alignment, and a cheap structural check would never see it. Two graders also named the same single wording fix, independently: P1-Q9s key says "only while an AVALANCHE is in motion" while Passage Bs opening produces booming with no dune and no avalanche at all, eight centimetres of poured sand sheared in a chute; the explanations own parenthetical concedes the gap. NOTHING DROPPED: 3 items came back solved by all three (L01, L05, L06) against 0.44 expected, p about 0.01 -- but every one is a DECLARED GUESS by all three at confidence 25-28, and AUTHORING-BRIEF 3d-bis is explicit that unanimity among declared guesses is not evidence. A SOLVER PRE-REGISTERED THE TEST THAT SETTLED THE ONE OPEN CHANNEL. Run-middle fired on 8 of 24 and all three solvers leaned on it; one stated before seeing any key that if L01, L02, L22 and L23 all keyed to the chain middle the channel was real. Result: L01 and L02 interior, L22 and L23 endpoints — 2 of 4, so NOT real, confirming its own null against its own instinct. A FOURTH LOOSE NULL WAS REFUTED, by the solver that built it: its first two nulls put the magnitude-outlier channel at z=+4.55 and z=+4.11, both artifacts because a null that preserves the item's range as a BOUND almost never realises both endpoints, while every real option set contains its own min and max by construction. Pinning the endpoints collapsed it to z=1.92. That joins sign-blind, decimal-blind and uniform-range on the list of nulls that manufactured a false z above 3 on this bank. 3 items came back unanimous against 0.38 expected, p=0.0069; under 3d-bis two carried a named mechanism and were dropped, and SAM11-14 was a declared guess by all three and was kept.

tells.verdict: Key letters re-dealt at draw time (AUTHORING-BRIEF 2b); the grade render dealt flat. check-stem-echo: options echo the stem at 10.0%, KEYS at 5.0%, margin -5.0 — the channel is ANTI-predictive here, so avoiding stem literals points away from keys. A grader nonetheless found the single instance behind that healthy aggregate, SAM11-19, where the key 0 is the literal from f(1) = 0; recorded per-item, not a batch defect. MY VERIFICATION OF THAT WAS ITSELF WRONG FIRST: my sweep reported ZERO key-echoes and would have contradicted the grader, because the regex excluded any number followed by a period — so every sentence-final value was invisible, which is exactly where "f(1) = 0." sits. Fixed, and it then reproduced both the checker's and the grader's numbers. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST IS A FAILURE MODE THE OPTIONS-ONLY GATE CANNOT SEE, and it is why the third grader was asked to look for it: TWO ITEMS ARE ANSWERABLE FROM THE STEM PLUS OPTION ARITHMETIC WITH NO ALGEBRA, and neither could ever appear in an options-only attack because both leaks REQUIRE the stem. SAM11-10 asks for the greater of two positive numbers differing by 3 whose squares sum to 65, and lists 7, 4, -4, 28: "positive" deletes -4, 28 squared alone exceeds 65, and the two survivors 4 and 7 ARE the solution pair, with the stem naming which one to take. SAM11-21 lists 20, 24, 10, 12 against a stem containing $240, 4 more people and $2 less: 10 and 12 differ by the 2, 20 and 24 differ by the 4, and "how many now" picks 20 by pattern-matching two printed numbers. Both verified directly and both dropped. The same grader independently measured "the key is the option with no arithmetic relation to the others" at 3 of 9 = 33.3%, noise against the 25% control — an independent confirmation of the options-only null from a different instrument.

Measured over 516 live maths items carrying an exact 2:1 pair: key is the smaller 24.8%, the larger 23.3%, neither 51.9% -- against chance of 25/25/50. Dead flat. Three of that solver's mechanism picks rested on nothing. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST IS NOT IN THE ATTACK AT ALL. The third grader was asked to hunt what an options-only run structurally cannot see, and found three items whose answer is reachable from the STEM plus option arithmetic with no mathematics: AM12I-02 gives the conversion formula in the stem and then lists 60.6, 81 and 170.6 as air temperatures, so 25 is pickable from weather familiarity; AM12G-01's midsegment must lie strictly between 12 and 19 and 15.5 is the ONLY option in that interval; AM12I-04's answer must lie in (7.5, 15) because more pumps means less time and the time cannot halve, and 9 is the only option there. Its own summary is the generalisation worth keeping: "every one of the six free eliminations I found is a bound or a sign argument on the stem's own numbers, and every one was invisible to an options-only run." Call the class BOUND FEASIBILITY. This is the SECOND consecutive batch where the with-source grader found real defects the attack could not -- on sat-adv-v11 it was two items whose option set contained its own solution pair -- which establishes that the options-only attack is half a gate and the complementary half has earned its place. All three dropped. Also dropped: AM12S-05, named by two graders as AM12S-07 in another costume (favourable measure over total measure, angles versus minutes). Recorded and NOT acted on: AM12I-02 and AM12S-04 are the same question -- substitute a value into a supplied linear rule -- sitting in DIFFERENT domains, which is exactly why a per-domain review cleared them; AM12G-03 is wholly contained in AM12G-10's hemisphere step; and per-domain authored key letters are lumpy (Geometry 6 of 10 C and zero D) though the draw re-deals them, so no student can reach it.

The brief that preceded this one asked for 12 items across four domains and was wrong, because blueprint-quotas.mjs had ACT Statistics at 0.17 (act-test.ts: [12,15]), IES at 0.17 ([20,20]) and the form at 48 questions (act-test.ts: 45). shape.verdict: Sandbox 11/11 recompute to their key; 33 of 33 distractor_solve entries recomputed, 0 mismatches. Denominators read, not the verdict -- the pre-fix file printed "Distractors: 0 of 0 recomputed across 11 item(s); 0 item(s) with a mismatch", a clean-looking pass over an empty population, which was only safe because the SHAPE lines above it were loud. BOTH GATE MECHANISMS BREAK-TESTED SEPARATELY, by the author and again independently by me: corrupting one solve body gives "Sandbox: 10/11" with the item named and its computed value printed, while the distractor line stays clean; corrupting one distractor body leaves the sandbox at 11/11 and reports "1 item(s) with a mismatch". So the two checks are independently live rather than one masking the other. All 44 bodies (11 solve + 33 distractor) were scanned for the degenerate case of a body that returns the answer literal with no arithmetic: ZERO. The author volunteered the two shortest bodies for inspection -- AM13I-10's '35.0' is (15+20).toFixed(1) and AM13I-12's '132.5' is (265/2).toFixed(1) -- and in both cases that is the named wrong procedure from the explanation computed from the stem's own numbers. 7 of 11 items needed explicit number formatting to match the option string exactly, including one where 22 x 17.40 x 48 evaluates to 18374.399999999998; grouping uses an inline regex rather than toLocaleString so it does not depend on the runtime's ICU data. Numeric hub: no derivational structure in any option set. NOTE that check-twin-options.mjs is NOT MEASURED on this batch and says so -- its 12-character guard excludes every numeric option set, a blind spot found today and now printed on the script's own face.

withsource.verdict: NOT RUN AS A SEPARATE GRADER PANEL. The difficulty labels in the qc file are the AUTHOR'S, not a panel's, and that is recorded rather than dressed up: on the last two batches independent graders read the author's labels as too hard and moved 5-8 items, so these labels should be treated as unverified. What did run with the stem visible is the author's own bound-feasibility audit, which is the instrument that decided the one drop. The author also cut three drafts before delivering: two duplicated live items found ONLY by scanning all 470 math rows rather than the 78 in this domain -- an inclusion-exclusion item matching a live Statistics and Probability row, and a part-hour-billing item matching a live Functions row, both of which a per-domain review would have cleared -- and one cut for sharing a proportion procedure with another item in its own batch.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, 12 candidates INTERLEAVED WITH 24 LIVE Integrating Essential Skills items in one file, 3 solvers, 108 picks, control derived at 25.0% from a perfect 9/9/9/9 global deal. CANDIDATES 6/36 = 16.7% (95% CI 7.9-31.9). LIVE CONTROL 23/72 = 31.9% (CI 22.3-43.4). -15.3 points, and the candidates sit BELOW the 25% control -- the solvers' machinery did not merely fail, it pointed away from the key. ALL THREE SOLVERS INDEPENDENTLY SCORED EXACTLY 2/12 = 16.7% on the candidates, against 29.2 / 37.5 / 29.2 on the shipped items. BASIS SPLIT: on candidates mechanism 22.2% vs declared guess 14.8%, both under control; on the SHIPPED items mechanism 37.0% vs guess 23.1%. The pre-registered rules bite on the live bank and not on the new items. The render was attacked before any solver ran: option-length means candidate 4.31 chars vs live control 2.94, gap 1.38, under the 3-char refusal threshold -- the Words in Context render earlier today had a 7.33-char gap and its strata were sortable, which is why this check exists. UNANIMITY: 1 of 12 candidates against 0.19 expected; 5 of 24 LIVE items against 0.38 expected.

tells.verdict: Key letters re-dealt at draw time. THE MOST USEFUL RESULT IS ABOUT THE SHIPPED BANK, NOT THIS BATCH: five live IES items were solved by all three solvers, three of them with a mechanism named 3/3, and two solvers independently described the same mechanism without seeing each other -- THE DISTRACTOR-GENERATION RECIPE IS INVERTIBLE. On live 1e82517b (43 / 2.52 / 33.48 / 38.52) the options reconstruct the stem outright: 2.52 is exactly 7% of 36, and 33.48 and 38.52 are 36 minus and plus 2.52, so base price and tax rate are readable off four numbers with no stem. Same shape on f797b020 (232/216/200/104) and 92b5c969 (16/15/60/3.75). One solver's generalisation is worth keeping: "it is not that one option is derived from the others, it is that the distractor-generation recipe is invertible. The more disciplined the brief about which slips to include, the more completely the option set encodes the stem." That is the rigid-brief corollary operating INSIDE a single item. Recorded against the live bank and NOT acted on: three items is a direction, and a distractor rewrite has inverted the tell every time it has been tried. THE ONE DROP IS NOT ON THE UNANIMITY: AM13I-05 (oven) was solved 3/3 but with mechanism 0/3, which under 3d-bis is three coins landing the same way and explicitly not grounds. It is dropped on an independent instrument -- the author's own bound-feasibility check found only 2 of 4 options survive the stem's bound, and named it the item they would drop first. TWO SOLVERS FLAGGED SHARED OPTION VALUES across AM13I-06 and AM13I-07 (675 and 702 in both) and asked whether the items are independent trials. Measured rather than believed: shared values touch 5 of 12 candidates; bootstrapping 2,000 draws of 12 from the 78 shipped IES items gives a live mean of 6.48 of 12 and P(live >= candidates) = 0.82. The shipped domain shares option values MORE than this batch does. A real pattern, correctly spotted, and not a defect. A SOLVER'S OWN HABIT, self-reported by the author before the attack: on 6 of 12 items the option set is a tight cluster of three plus a far outlier and the outlier is never the key, which would take a solver from 25% to 33% on half the batch. 0 of 6 is p~0.18, not significant, and it arises naturally because "multiplied instead of divided" errors land far away -- the attack result at 16.7% is the measurement that settles it.
